title: Adjacent transitions of second-ideal algebraizations lift and induce quotients
statement: Let X be a Noetherian scheme and I,K quasi-coherent ideals. Let M be a coherent I-adic formal module [def-weil-pbc-coherent-formal-module]. Assume completion on V(K^r) with extended ideal I is an equivalence for every r ≥ 1. For each e ≥ 0 let G_e be a coherent module on V(K^(e+1)), let F_e be its closed pushforward, and fix an isomorphism β_e from the I-completion of F_e to the system (M_n/K^(e+1)M_n)_n. Then K^(e+1)F_e=0, and there exists t_e:F_(e+1)→F_e such that (i) an isomorphism q_e:F_(e+1)/K^(e+1)F_(e+1)→F_e satisfies π_K q_e=t_e, and (ii) completion(t_e) β_e=β_(e+1) B(e+1→e), where B is the double quotient system and B(e+1→e) its induced adjacent K-transition.

source.place: Tag 088A, construction of G_e and their adjacent quotient maps

proof.text: Closed pushforward from V(K^(e+1)) is annihilated by its ideal. The affine section formula for recursive ideal powers identifies this with K^(e+1)F_e=0.

Both adjacent pushforwards are killed by K^(e+2). Use the closed-immersion equivalence and the assumed completion equivalence on V(K^(e+2)); their composite is fully faithful on these modules. Lift β_(e+1) followed by the adjacent transition and β_e inverse to t_e. By construction its completion satisfies (ii).

Annihilation of the target factors t_e through the K^(e+1)-quotient. Coherence of this quotient follows from formalCompletionSystem_coherent. Interchange quotients by I and K, and use the iterated quotient identity, to see that completion of the factor is an isomorphism. Both objects of the factor are killed by K^(e+1); completion on V(K^(e+1)) reflects isomorphisms. Its factor is therefore q_e, with (i) by construction.
